content.title: About
content.content: French or Catalina Dressing is a flavorful sauce made from mayonnaise, tomato sauce, vinegar, sugar and spices. It combines sweet‑sour notes with a mild tang, making it popular for salads, seafood, and chicken dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dressing was first created in the United States in the mid‑20th century and quickly became a staple of California cuisine.
The name “Catalina” comes from Catalina Island, where the sauce was often served in seaside restaurants.
There are several recipe variations: some add mustard, others include anchovies for extra depth.
It is frequently used as a grill marinade as well as in sandwiches and wraps.
In Russia the sauce is often called “French dressing,” although the original recipe is American.

items.title: Source of vitamin A
items.content: The tomato component provides vitamin A, important for vision and immune function.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Vinegar and tomatoes add vitamin C, an antioxidant that supports cell protection.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: The mayonnaise base supplies monounsaturated fats, which can be part of a heart‑healthy diet when consumed in moderation.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Vinegar may aid digestion and improve nutrient absorption.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Tomatoes and spices are rich in antioxidants that help combat free radicals.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: A mayonnaise‑based dressing is calorie‑dense; excessive intake can contribute to weight gain.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Mayonnaise contains eggs, which can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Sugar and salt levels
items.content: The recipe includes sugar and salt, which may be undesirable for low‑sodium or low‑sugar diets.

items.title: Preservatives in commercial versions
items.content: Store‑bought dressings may contain artificial preservatives and flavorings that some people prefer to avoid.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: French or Catalina Dressing works well as a salad dressing, a dip for seafood or chicken, and as a spread in sandwiches and wraps. It can also be mixed into marinades for meat or used as a dip for vegetable sticks.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the dressing refrigerated at 1 °C–4 °C in a sealed container. Once opened, it is usually good for 1–2 weeks. Discard if the smell, color, or taste changes.
